events.text_en: Phó Tiêu Tương hangs a chain of nine bronze cups from the eaves of her tower on the cone. It rings when it rains, and she sits under it.
A drummer's boy of Kích Cổ Đường, sixteen, walks up the cone with Khải Lôi's storm notes in his head. Phó Tiêu Tương takes him in and names him Văn Lôi, he who hears the thunder.
On Văn Lôi Đài, where the rain turns to thunder, Nhiếp Văn Lôi writes the thunder into the founder's chain: the Văn Lôi Kinh.
In the empty storm camp of Nghênh Lôi Trại the Tower finds Khải Lôi's Heavenly Tribulation Scripture and a third of the Gate's own canon.
The guest master Văn Hải Khô dies in seclusion at the Tower. The Tower records a qi deviation, and his Hollow Tide Scripture passes to the head.
Lệ Tiêu Hồn writes the vault law: a life lamp for every sworn member of the Tower, and none for the head; a lamp may be put out from afar only by the master lamp and the shears together.
With the vein kept, the Tower builds its new guard on Thần Cổ Phong above the ashes of Thủ Lôi Bảo, and names the guardhouse for Tạ Thiết Trụ.
At the pass of Đan Sơn Mạch, Kỷ Vãn Tình holds the Tower's rear guard until the Pivot's arrays close. Four of her people come out with the wounded.
Thính Vũ Lâu carries its halls east from the cone to Thần Cổ Phong. Quan Vũ Thanh stays in the founder's tower with the founder's chain, and the old seat becomes the Rain Tower.
Thạch Liên Hoàn casts and Lệ Tiêu Hồn lays the Iron Rain array, a bronze chain from the new seat down to Kinh Lôi Mạch; the soul vaults move into the vein.
Xuyên Lâm Môn protests the Tower's seat among its mines. Its head sends his nephew Úc Đả Diệp to Thần Cổ Phong as surety.
A Xuyên Lâm-born disciple deserts the Tower for the Gate. The vault keeper Ninh Tịch Đăng refuses to cut his wick, and he lives.
